records.researcher_notes: GEM does not list this plant. In case PU-24-342 at the North Dakota Public Service Commission, Northern States Power, doing business as Xcel Energy, must build a gas plant of at least 200 MW in eastern North Dakota. Its supplemental filing of August 5, 2025 says it bid 447 MW of firm dispatchable capacity directly adjacent to the Xcel Energy Bison Substation in Harmony Township, Cass County, about 10 miles west of Fargo. The project chart in that filing shows service in the third quarter of 2032. Xcel says it has already spent about 1.6 million dollars on site design, surveys, land options and MISO study payments. The timeline in the filing has the revised plant proposed in 2027, an interconnection agreement and a certificate filing in 2029, construction in 2030 and service late in 2032. The commission order of October 23, 2025 moved the deadline to December 31, 2032. MISO queue entry J3163 is the same project: Northern States Power, Cass County, 481 MW simple cycle combustion turbine, connecting at Bison. The filing gives 447 MW, so that is the capacity used. The status is announced because no certificate application or interconnection agreement exists yet. The point is the Bison Substation, so the location is approximate. The name is chosen to keep it apart from Basin Electric's Bison Generation Station in Williams County. GEM's Xcel Fargo power plant record is a cancelled 400 MW project from an earlier plan. A separate question card covers it.

records.researcher_notes: Critical Data House plans a data center campus called Project Fighting Pike on the north side of Williston, in Williams County. The City of Williston approved the plat and planned unit development on March 25, 2025. The city planning staff report of March 10, 2025 says each building will have 20 to 25 diesel backup generators, with the Caterpillar 3516E named as the model. A noise study filed with the city, by RWDI and dated February 7, 2025, is firmer. It gives twenty-five Caterpillar 3516 series diesel generators for each of the seven buildings, 175 in all, each with its own 3,000 kVA transformer. Neither document gives a power rating for each engine. A 3,000 kVA transformer per engine points to about 2.4 MW each, so Phase 1 alone would be about 120 MW and the whole campus about 420 MW. Both are far above the 50 MW threshold for a backup generator fleet. Capacity per engine is left blank and asked as a question. The units follow the three phases in the noise study. The status is pre-construction because the city has approved the project and the company is still seeking clear title to the land. A Williston Herald article of September 17, 2026 says work will start once the title is cleared and the campus could run in late 2028 or early 2029. Phase 1 would run on an existing 115 kV line of Mountrail-Williams Electric Cooperative. Later phases need a new 345 kV line that the North Dakota Public Service Commission would site. The staff report mentions a gas line on the site but does not say what it serves. Not found: a state air permit, a commission case for the 345 kV line, or a power rating for the engines. The owner is Critical Data House, LLC, named on the plat and in the news. The staff report spells the applicant Critical Data Housing, LLC. Neither name is in the GEM entity list. An earlier version of this batch put the campus on the watch list because only the TV news story had been read. The city planning records name the generator fleet.
